rubric: Each feature is split into concrete steps. A verified step (backed by an automated test, the app's end-to-end self-test, or a measured benchmark) counts 1. An implemented-but-unverified step counts 0.5. Planned steps count 0. Feature % = step score ÷ steps. Overall parity weights features by priority (P0 = 3, P1 = 2, P2 = 1). A reference DAW's parity covers only the features that DAW has.

screenshots.caption: Arrangement: rainbow track colors from green, gain and pan knobs, M/S chips, vertical meters, control bar in the title bar.
Recording and MIDI: R chips arm tracks, each header shows its input (IN 1 or MIDI), the record button sits next to Play, and MIDI clips show their notes.
Device panel: the selected track's plug-ins (Apple's AUDelay and AUPeakLimiter here) with a controller of knobs per plug-in; Edit Controls chooses the parameters.
Piano roll: notes shaded by velocity, a velocity lane, bars-and-beats grid; every gesture is one undo step.

Warm Analog: the same layout as hardware — LED buttons, metal knobs with LED rings, LED ladder meters, a VFD position display, lit scribble-strip track names, and plug-ins as rack units joined by patch cables.
Settings: choose an appearance and whether saved projects copy their audio.
Command palette (⌘K): fuzzy search over every command, with its menu location and shortcut.
Empty project: a drop zone with Import Audio, Open Project, and Migration Assistant.
First run: pick the DAW you're coming from. Dalnok adopts its shortcuts and vocabulary.
Concept Guide: each Logic, Ableton or REAPER idea, its Dalnok equivalent, and its status.
⌘K understands other DAWs' words: 'bounce' finds Export Mix.
Plug-ins: installed VST3, CLAP and Audio Unit plug-ins with type and scan status (shown filtered to Apple's built-in units). Loading them onto tracks comes next.

features.name: Track color system
features.why: Color is how you find 'the vocals'. It should be beautiful, consistent and stable.
steps: Rainbow gradient from green (OKLCH, equal brightness, alternating lightness for color-blind users)
Clips, waveforms, gain and pan derive from the track color; text contrast picked automatically
Custom colors and Recolor Tracks as Gradient
Group or section colors tint their member tracks
features.evidence: TrackColors tests; self-test checks the hue progression and the color menus.

features.name: Pro track-header controls
features.why: Faders and knobs should feel like an instrument, not a settings page.
steps: Gain knob with audio taper, live post-fader level halo, value bubble, reset, fine-adjust, scroll and arrow keys
Labeled rotary pan knob with center detent
M/S chips with pro state colors; vertical stereo meters
Record-arm chip and input selector on every track
features.evidence: Self-test checks live gain-halo levels, drives both knobs with synthesized mouse events, then undoes. Accessibility: knobs and faders are sliders with values and increment/decrement; arrangement clips and launcher scenes/slots are exposed as buttons with track, position, length and state, and the self-test presses a clip through its accessibility element to select it. Not yet checked with VoiceOver itself.

Windows paths and moved project folders resolved
Tested on real projects (6/6, all audio found)
Playback rate and pitch (time-stretched to match)

Live path types, Backup/ sets, moved archives (95% of 6,929 real file references resolved)
Warped clips: piecewise stretch per warp marker; Re-Pitch and transpose
Session clips, take lanes, MIDI, devices
features.evidence: AbletonImport tests; local survey of the owner's Live 11/12 sets. abletonWarpMarkersBecomePiecewiseStretch; a real set with 334 stretched clips imports in 1.7 s.

steps: Open supports Logic project packages and asks before import
Final Cut Pro XML (Logic's documented export) import
.logicx: metadata, audio files, region trims (30 real projects)
.logicx: audio region placement and track names/order
.logicx: mixer settings, routing, take folders, MIDI and automation
features.evidence: LogicImport generated-fixture tests cover region IDs, placement, names and order; FcpxmlImport tests cover XML.

features.evidence: Self-test: presets checked for expected keys and collisions; finder scan; welcome flow.

features.name: Old-DAW vocabulary and Concept Guide

steps: ⌘K matches other DAWs' terms (bounce, region, collect all and save…)
Planned features appear with their status
features.evidence: Self-test palette and guide checks.

features.name: Low-latency playback engine
features.why: Everything else sits on it: glitch-free, low-latency playback under load.
steps: Core Audio output with an allocation-free, lock-free callback
Real-time safety checked by the compiler (and in CI)
Click-free play, pause, and seek (5 ms fades)
Background rendering for stretched clips (audio thread stays copy-only)
Disk streaming for very long sessions
features.evidence: LivePath tests (mutation-checked click detection); rt-effects CI job; dalnok-cli bench: 256 tracks at 3% of the real-time budget, single-threaded.

features.name: Audio device selection
features.why: Pros switch between an interface (e.g. Scarlett) and speakers or headphones constantly.
steps: Fall back to System Default when a device is unplugged
features.evidence: Devices tests; self-test switches devices through the Audio menu.

features.name: Sample-rate handling
features.why: Mixed-rate material and devices must just work.
steps: Resample imported audio to the project rate
Rescale project positions when opened at another rate
Convert when the device runs at another rate
Choose the project sample rate in the UI
features.evidence: loadResamplesToEngineRate (pitch preserved), loadingAtAnotherSampleRateRescalesPositions.

features.name: Audio recording
features.why: Core of the owner's workflow. Recording integrity matters more than anything else.
steps: Same-device capture to a recoverable spool (Scarlett Solo: 120 s take, 0 dropped frames)
Record-arm tracks (R chip, ⌃R) and choose the input channel
Record to the armed track: one undoable take, saved in the project and reopened
Take journal; process-kill recovery with every recovered sample exact
Interrupted takes are never placed; the valid part is saved and reported
Latency-compensated placement (device-reported latency; loopback measurement pending)
Punch in and out (autopunch range; sample-accurate)
Multiple armed audio tracks, each recording its own input (one take each, one undo step)
features.evidence: RecordingTests: bit-exact take contents, latency placement, undo/redo, save and reopen, interrupted takes, journal recovery and monitoring on the simulated input. scripts/ci/record-crash.sh kills a real-time take at three points and verifies every recovered sample. App self-test records through the real menus. Scarlett Solo 4th Gen at 44.1 kHz: 10 s and 120 s takes via dalnok-cli record, 0 dropped frames. Latency compensation uses the device's reported figures (1,186 frames on the Solo) and has not been checked with a loopback measurement; monitoring was not checked by ear. PunchTests: a mid-block punch window records exactly its frames, count-in pre-roll starts the take at the record point (also when requested while playing), and count-in clicks stop at the record point; the self-test records with count-in and autopunch through the Transport menu. MultiInputTests: two armed tracks on inputs 1 and 3 each get exactly their input's samples, one undo removes both, and a failed multi-track take recovers one file per track (repeatably); the self-test records two armed tracks through the menus. Not yet run on the Scarlett with both inputs.

features.name: Comping and take folders
features.why: Logic's swipe comping is the fastest way to build a vocal. Required before the owner switches.
steps: Cycle recording into takes (one take per pass, a take folder per armed track)
Take lanes (in the Takes window; not yet expanded inside the arrangement)
Swipe comping, click a take for all of it, one undo step per swipe
Make a take folder from overlapping clips
features.evidence: TakeFolderTests: a 2.5-pass cycle take becomes three takes with exact offsets, the newest pass plays where it exists, a comp change plays the chosen take's exact samples and undoes in one step, invalid comps are rejected, folders survive save/reopen (format 7), and a folder made from two clips comps them. App self-test: cycle recording through the menus makes a folder of 3 takes, double-clicking the comp opens the Takes window, a swipe across Take 1 and a click on Take 2 change the comp, and undo restores it. Crossfades are 256-frame equal-power fades into the following piece; not yet judged by ear. Edits to comp pieces in the arrangement are replaced on the next comp change.

features.name: Non-destructive clip editing
features.why: Moving, trimming, and splitting audio is most of editing.
steps: Trim either edge without touching the source audio
Fades and crossfades (linear and equal power)
features.evidence: UndoAndEditing and Fades tests (crossfade weights checked numerically); self-test drives real drags, fade handles, and menu items. GUI self-test verifies shift-selection, marquee selection across tracks, group nudge/drag/delete and undo; group drag is horizontal only.

features.name: Undo and redo
features.why: Safe experimentation.
steps: Named undo for every edit (500 steps)
A whole drag is one undo step
Undo history saved with the project
features.evidence: everyEditIsUndoableAndRedoable, groupsCollapseIntoOneStep, gainUndoRestoresAudio.

features.name: Grid and snapping
features.why: Musical edits land on the beat.
steps: Bars and beats grid, following tempo and meter changes
Snap to clip edges and transients
features.evidence: Self-test: move snapped to grid.

features.name: Flex Time and warping
features.why: Fix timing and match tempos without re-recording.
steps: Imported warp markers and playback rates play correctly
Flex/warp markers editable in the clip
features.evidence: TimeStretch tests measure pitch (±1%) and level (±1.5 dB) on rendered output; mutation-checked. Self-test ⌥-drag.

features.name: Flex Pitch (note-level pitch editing)
features.why: Vocal tuning inside the DAW.
features.evidence: transposeKeepsLength: +12 semitones measured at 880 Hz with length unchanged.

features.name: Spectral view and repair
features.why: Remove clicks and noise visually.
features.evidence: Planned for Phase 6.

features.name: Multitrack arrangement
features.why: The main canvas.
steps: Track reorder (drag or menu), rename, and delete
Duplicate and hide tracks; track height and vertical zoom; zoom to selection
Cycle region: sample-exact loop playback, ruler band, C
features.evidence: topClipWinsWhenOverlapping; screenshots. MarkerTests and GUI self-test cover markers and navigation; ClipCopyTests and GUI self-test cover duplicate track, hide/show and zoom controls.

features.name: Clip launching (unified with the timeline)
features.why: Sketching and performance without a separate session copy of every track.
steps: Launcher slots on every track, beside the timeline lane (View > Clip Launcher, cmd-L)
Quantized launch (next bar, sample-exact) and looping; stop back to the arrangement
Record a launcher performance to the timeline
Follow actions (next slot or stop after N loops, exact at loop ends)
Drag a slot clip onto the timeline
Record into slots (trimmed to whole bars); drag timeline clips into slots
features.evidence: LauncherTests: launching while playing switches exactly on the next bar and loops every clip length, stopping returns to the arrangement on a later bar, launching while stopped starts the transport, exports play the arrangement only, scenes launch every filled track. App self-test: View > Clip Launcher, clicking an empty slot copies the selected clip, clicking launches it and clicking again stops it on the bar, undo. LauncherFollowAndRecord: next-slot and stop follow actions switch on the exact loop end; recording a performance writes loop passes into the arrangement from the launch frame (one undo step). Self-test: follow action from the slot menu, dragging a slot onto the timeline, Transport > Record Launcher to Arrangement. RecordIntoSlot: a take started mid-bar lands in the target slot as the one whole bar it covers (offset 86,000, length 96,000, sample-exact), nothing stays in the arrangement, one undo removes it. Self-test: dragging an arrangement clip into a slot copies it and leaves the clip in place; an empty slot's menu sets and clears the record target. Launch quantization is one bar.

features.name: Track volume, pan, mute, solo
features.why: Basic mixing.
features.evidence: gainInDecibels, monoPanIsCompensatedConstantPower, stereoPanIsBalance, gainChangesAreSmoothed. soloSilencesOthersAndUndoes, soloOnTheLivePathIsSmoothed.

features.name: Metering
features.why: See levels and catch clipping.
features.evidence: metersReportPostFaderPeaksAndReset; self-test checks the meters during playback.

features.name: Mixer window
features.why: Logic's mixer is a switching requirement.
steps: Channel strips: output, sends, pan, vertical fader with meter, mute/solo/arm, name (View > Mixer, X)
features.evidence: App self-test: View > Mixer shows a strip per track, Track > New Bus adds a strip, the strip's output menu and + Send route a track, a fader drag lowers the volume as one undo step, and deleting a bus removes its sends. Reviewed in both themes with --uiwalk (including mid-drag). Inserts are still edited in the device panel.

features.name: Buses, sends, and sidechains
features.why: Reverb sends, parallel processing, ducking.
steps: Aux buses and track outputs (feedback loops rejected)
Solo follows routing (soloing a bus keeps its sources; soloing a source keeps its buses)
Sidechain inputs (VST3 auxiliary bus; source chosen on the device card)
Sidechain inputs for Audio Units (second input bus) and CLAP (second audio port)
Plugin delay compensation (tracks, buses and sends; live and exports)
features.evidence: DelayCompensationTests (test VST3 that delays by exactly its reported 300 frames): a latent insert stays sample-aligned with other tracks, a latent bus and a send into it arrive together with the direct paths, and live playback puts the impulse exactly at the playhead. RoutingTests (offline renders, 1e-4 tolerance): output through a bus applies its fader and balance pan; post-fader and pre-fader sends add the expected levels; mute silences pre-fader sends; chained buses; solo through routing; feedback and clips on buses rejected; deleting a bus returns its sources to the master and undo restores the routing; routing survives save/reopen (format 5) and a looping file is rejected. TSan clean on the live render path tests. Live MIDI input played while stopped still goes straight to the master.

features.name: Track stacks and groups
features.why: Organization and summing.
steps: Summing stacks (stack bus, members routed in, fader and plug-ins act on all)
features.evidence: TrackStacks engine test: the stack sums its members, its fader scales only them, order and routing, collapse flag, ungroup and undo. stacksNest engine test: nested routing and faders (1e-4 tolerance), ordering, ungroup, deletion, undo and save/reopen. App self-test: create, collapse, expand and undo nested stacks; mixer output menus retain identically named stacks.

features.name: Automation
features.why: Movement in a mix.
steps: Volume and pan automation drawn over each lane (View > Show Automation, A): add, move, delete points
Plug-in parameter automation (block-rate; plug-in window > Automate in Arrangement)
Write modes (read, touch, latch) for volume and pan from header knobs and mixer faders
Smooth playback on a fixed 32-frame ramp grid; live playback equals the export
features.evidence: AutomationTests: volume follows the fader taper between points (exact values midway and a quarter of the way), held before and after, pan automation, mute still applies, live playback in 333-frame blocks matches the offline export sample for sample, save/reopen (format 6, also at 44.1 kHz) and undo. App self-test adds, drags and deletes points through the timeline and clears a lane from the Track menu. Not yet: plug-in parameter automation, write modes (touch/latch), automation following clip moves.

features.name: VST3 plugin hosting
features.why: The first plugin format (owner's choice). The SDK is MIT-licensed.
steps: Discover bundles and read moduleinfo metadata without loading code
Validation scan in a separate process with timeout and cache (dalnok-scan)
Load and process: insert effects and instruments, sample-accurate notes, live MIDI
Save and restore plugin state; a missing plugin keeps its state and is bypassed
Plugin editor window (the plug-in's own interface)
Parameter changes from editors and Dalnok reach the processor
features.evidence: scripts/ci/plugin-host.sh builds a test VST3 (gain effect, note-driven synth) and checks exact gain, a bit-exact passthrough null test, note on/off on the exact sample across block boundaries, live input, undo/redo, state through save and reopen, and a missing plugin keeping its state (also under ThreadSanitizer). Vital (VST3, third-party) loads as an instrument through the command catalog and renders its notes offline (0.28 RMS during clips, 0.0007 in the gap). Offline renders and exports use separate plugin instances. The app adds and removes VST3 plug-ins from Audio ▸ Plug-ins and the track menu (self-test with the test plugin). Parameters: the test plug-in's processor sees changes only through process(); they apply live from the next block and in exports (replayed into the export's instance). Vital's editor opened inside Dalnok's plug-in window (1440×907 pt, checked by a window capture), with 2,855 parameters in the generic panel; editor edits were not exercised automatically.

features.name: Generic in-DAW plugin parameter panel
features.why: Owner request: edit any plugin's parameters without opening its window.
steps: Parameter list with sliders and the plug-in's own value text
Device panel with a custom controller per plug-in (choose parameters; saved; undoable)
Automate and map from the panel
features.evidence: App self-test with the test plug-in: the panel lists its parameter, sets it, shows the plug-in's text, and filters. Works for any VST3 (Vital: 2,855 parameters). Device panel: self-test turns a knob, edits the controller (one undo step), undoes it, and checks the knob follows changes made elsewhere.

features.name: Audio Unit hosting
features.why: Logic users own AU plugins.
steps: List registered Audio Units by type (no instantiation)
Instantiate and initialize in a separate process (latency, tail, parameter count)
Load and process effects and instruments on tracks
features.evidence: AudioUnitHosting tests with Apple's units: AUDelay dry-only null within 1e-5, wet output delayed 50 ms, state through save/reopen; DLSMusicDevice silent before and sounding during a clip note. App self-test drives AUDelay and AUPeakLimiter in the device panel.

features.name: CLAP hosting
features.why: Open standard with per-note modulation.
steps: Read plugin descriptors in a separate process
features.evidence: PluginDiscovery tests; ClapHosting test (plugin-host.sh) loads a test CLAP gain: exact 0.5 gain, parameter set and display text, automation at 0.25, state through save/reopen.

features.name: Plugin crash protection
features.why: One bad plugin must not take down a session.
steps: Out-of-process hosting (plugins currently run in the app process)
features.evidence: scripts/ci/plugin-scan.sh: a plugin that aborts is reported as crashed and one that never returns is killed after the timeout.

features.name: Stock effects (EQ, compressor, reverb, delay)
features.why: A complete mix without buying plugins.
features.evidence: Planned.

features.name: Sampler and instruments
features.why: Composing needs sounds out of the box.
features.evidence: MidiTests measure pitch (440 Hz within 0.5 Hz), onset, release and velocity scaling; a mutation check confirmed the pitch test catches a 2 Hz error. Most instruments are expected to come from plugins (ADR-0009), so the stock set stays small.

features.name: MIDI tracks and piano roll
features.why: Composition.
steps: MIDI source discovery and independently tested MIDI 1 message parser
Instrument tracks and MIDI clips (undo, split, trim, save and reopen)
Core MIDI input ports feed the armed instrument live (virtual-source test)
MIDI recording into a clip (block-accurate timing)
Piano roll: add, move, resize, delete, transpose and nudge notes; one undo step per gesture
Marquee selection and keyboard step entry
Note preview while stopped for unarmed tracks, scale and chord tools
Recorded and checked with a real keyboard
features.evidence: MidiTests: recording, quantize, persistence, split rendering, and a Core MIDI virtual source driving the instrument through a real input port (TSan clean). The app self-test plays live MIDI through the running device, records a note through the menus and quantizes. Input events are stamped at the start of the audio callback that receives them, so timing is up to one buffer late. The Arturia MiniLab has not been played into a recording yet. The piano roll is driven by the GUI self-test with synthesized mouse and key events (add, drag, resize, velocity, transpose, nudge, delete, undo, select all). GUI self-test also covers marquee and keyboard step entry. GUI self-test checks group movement at pitch and time boundaries.

features.name: Tempo and time signature
features.why: Bars and beats, click track, tempo changes.
steps: Project tempo and meter, edited in the control bar (saved; drives quantize, ruler and grid)
Constant-tempo edits preserve MIDI beat placement while audio stays time-locked
Bars-and-beats ruler, grid, snapping and position display
Tempo changes (tempo map): MIDI stays on its beats, audio keeps its time
Meter changes (ruler, grid, snapping, metronome accents)
Count-in (one bar of clicks; take starts at the record point)
features.evidence: MidiTests (tempo validation, persistence, quantize grid) and Metronome tests (click on the exact beat sample, 1.6 kHz accent / 1 kHz beat, silent in offline renders). The self-test edits tempo and meter in the control bar, checks the bars-and-beats position display and toggles the metronome, confirming it reaches the output past the end of the session. Offline-render MIDI tests verify tempo edits, split-note continuity, undo and reopening. TempoMaps tests: notes crossing a tempo change keep their beats (exact frames), clips after it move, quantize follows the map, the metronome clicks on the exact samples and accents the new bars across tempo and meter changes, maps survive save/reopen (also at another sample rate) and damaged maps are rejected. The self-test adds, edits and removes tempo and time-signature changes through the Transport menu and control bar, and checks the ruler, LCD and control bar follow the playhead. Tempo changes are steps (no ramps); importers bring in the first tempo only.

features.name: Command palette and discoverability
features.why: Owner's top complaint about Logic: features hidden in menus.
steps: Runs through the same validation as menus
Ranks recent and frequent commands higher
features.evidence: Self-test: palette finds 'Split at Playhead' from 'splt plhd' and runs it.

features.name: Scripting, macros, and the action system
features.why: REAPER-level customization, which Logic lacks.
features.evidence: CommandCatalog tests; dalnok-cli command and render-project.

features.name: Customizable keyboard shortcuts
features.why: Speed.
features.evidence: ⌘T split, ⌘B export, ⌥⌘N new track, ⌘⌫ delete track, Space, ↩, ⌘K. Self-test: Space types into text fields instead of triggering Play.

features.name: Themes (including analog)
features.why: Owner wants many options, including a high-end analog look.
steps: Graphite dark theme with documented tokens (4-pt grid, type scale)
Warm Analog as a hardware overhaul: LED lenses, metal knobs with LED rings, LED ladder meters, VFD, faceplates, scribble strips, patch-cabled rack units (same layout and controls)
Motion: lit chip glow and press, knob glide on undo, record pulse, metronome tick, selection glide, fades (respects Reduce Motion)
features.evidence: UI audit, reviewed screenshots, and app self-tests in both themes. Live switching: the self-test changes the theme in Settings both ways from each theme; the main window is rebuilt in the new style with the same project, track colours and undo history, settings stays open (a change during recording waits for a relaunch). Warm Analog extras: vintage track palette, tape reels (self-test checks they wind with the playhead), splice-bay Takes window, lit-pin piano roll, walnut mixer cheeks. VoiceOver and all auxiliary windows are not yet verified. Motion: the self-test checks knob glide, record pulse, palette fade, analog lamp warm-up and cool-down, patch-cable settling, and Reduce Motion. Animation timing has not been visually reviewed in motion. Warm Analog: the self-test passes all checks in that theme (including the patch-cable count for a two-plug-in chain); visual review from snapshots; see 06 - Design/Warm Analog. Warm Analog control-bar tape strip: GUI self-test checks play, pause, winding and return to zero; real input on a generated project also confirmed PLAY, FF and RTZ.

features.name: Audio import
features.why: Getting material in.
steps: Drag and drop onto the window
WAV, AIFF, CAF, MP3, AAC, ALAC, and FLAC via Core Audio
Copy media into the project folder
features.evidence: Self-test import; WAV and AIFF covered by tests; other formats rely on Core Audio decoders and aren't tested yet. saveCopyingMediaMakesProjectSelfContained.

features.name: Project save, open, and recovery
features.why: Never lose work.
steps: Moved project folders still find their audio
Periodic recovery snapshots and manual restore after process crash
features.evidence: Persistence and TwoPhaseLoad tests; self-test save, New, and reopen. relinkBringsOfflineClipsBack; self-test relinks by searching a folder. Recovery snapshot and manual restore are covered by the app self-test; scripts/ci/recovery-smoke.sh verifies automatic timing and reload after force-stopping an isolated process. Power-loss durability and automatic recovery prompting remain unverified.

features.name: Export and bounce
features.why: Deliver the mix.
features.evidence: renderToWavRoundTrips; self-test export decodes to the session length.

features.name: DAWproject interchange
features.why: No lock-in. Move projects between DAWs.
steps: Export DAWproject (tracks, audio and MIDI clips, fades, warp-marker stretch, volume, pan, mute, solo, outputs, sends, audio files)
Import DAWproject (audio clips, fades, warp-marker stretch, mixer basics; MIDI, plug-ins, automation reported)
Plug-in states, automation and MIDI import through DAWproject
features.evidence: DawprojectTests: a generated project exports to a ZIP that /usr/bin/unzip lists and CRC-checks; importing it back restores clip positions, offsets, fades, a 0.5x stretch, track gain and pan, and renders the same audio within 1e-5; MIDI and submix routing are reported. Self-test: File > Export as DAWproject... and the export imports back with every audio clip. Times are written in seconds; one tempo and time signature.

features.name: Real-time safety guarantees
features.why: A differentiator: dropout-free by construction, not by luck.
steps: Compile-time nonblocking checks on the audio path
Enforced in CI with a negative test
features.evidence: scripts/ci/rt-effects.sh; mutation-checked click tests.

features.name: Fast startup and small footprint
features.why: REAPER's speed is a big part of its appeal.
steps: Baseline measured (323 KB binary, 3,051× realtime offline render)
features.evidence: 08 - Testing and Benchmarks/Baseline 2026-11-16.
